text_fidelity_a:
Asus Nexus 7 2B32 7-Inch 32 GB Tablet, Black (2013 Model) 7 May 2014: Thanks to Google's omission of full USB OTG function, file transfers are frustrating & sometimes impossible. When I return home, I'm rooting it.

After 24 hours, I like it. It's a little different from my Galaxy Player 5 inch. The extra processor speed is nice. So is the combination of the light weight and larger screen. The GP5 was getting bogged down by software bloat. It fits nicely in my old K3 case. So far, so good.

...and it works with my Targus Bluetooth keyboard. Actually, it works better than it does with the GP5. The Samsung has some key-mapping problems, probably due to Gingerbread.

As to reading, I happened to be starting a novel the other day, and started it on the Nexus 7. I had no problem. I did keep the brightness on 'Auto', so the light level of the screen matched the ambient light. With the GP5, matching light levels was a little chancy, so I had a bit more eyestrain. (Of course the extra 2" of screen have no bearing on that, right?)

I did try the freebie 'La Luna' video that Google gives away. It watched fine on the 7" screen. The thing I really like is that there is a 7" screen in the weight of a past-technology 5" package. I owned a Nook color for 13 days, but took it back because of the weight and balance. It just wasn't comfortable to hold.

I haven't tried any significant music listening. I suspect I'll still prefer my Clip+ for that. The Nexus is a little large for that purpose. I also haven't tried the camera in any particular serious way. A selfie and a picture of my cat isn't much of a trial. Again, I'll probably use a purpose-made camera for real pictures. I also haven't explored portability yet. In the case, it's a bit bulky for easy transport, whereas the GP5 fits in my pocket next to my cell phone. I probably won't put the N7 in my pocket without a case. It's a little large and fragile seeming for that.

...As to the camera, it's OK, the image quality is fine, but a 7" tablet just isn't a good ergonomic platform for picture taking. This is the best from an afternoon at Mass Audubon's Ipswich River Wildlife Sanctuary.

Picture is available at:
MobileRead Forums > E-Book Readers > Android Devices>Nexus 7 2013 1st Impressions

...And I still prefer my Clip+ for music. I hand to hunt around the Android store for a decent player for my collection which includes WMAs as well as MP3s. Google does not play WMAs (cue prissy, superior sniff). I settled on Poweramp, not because it was perfect, but because it was the first one I came to that was good enough. I just want to listen to some music, people, not commit my soul to a single, ringing, crystalline-pure music player that rules them all. Sheesh.

Someday I may do a better review, too. All of the usual things about tablets are at worst adequate on the N7.

Oh, one piece of free advice, worth every penny you paid: Don't go hog wild buying really great accessories. Shop around. A $3 wire easel from a craft store will make a fine desk stand. I have one at work and one at home. A chopstick and a binder clip will do in a pinch. Also, there are good $10 EVA zip cases that will protect your N7 for transport. They don't have to be purpose built. My old K3 had a case that loosely fits the N7 (freebie!) and my KPW1 lives in a similar case. As to ear buds, the candy-colored $5 ones in the bin at the cash register at WalGreens are my favorite, and you never misplace them, because candy-colored.
text_fidelity_b: Asus Nexus 7 2B32 7-Inch 32 GB Tablet, Black (2013 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display I have unusual needs for the Kindle Touch. It is my study device. As an autodidact moving along in years I found that lugging a lot of textbooks/reference books/dictionaries around was getting in the way of learning. Sure, I can use a laptop for lots of online material to study but when I'm comfortable in my easy chair and the laptop is in the other room I just don't want to get up. Enter the Touch. I am reading philosophy and studying Latin on my own. I have loaded the Touch up with many free or low cost books on Aristotle and St. Thomas Aquinas. I have many personal Latin documents, some Latin readers and texts, Interlinear translation of the Douay-Rheims Bible, etc. Now I discover that I can save web pages in html file format and convert them to mobi format for the Touch and end up with "live" links to hundreds of web pages I am interested in using in my studies. I have sent these documents to the Touch either using the email forwarding capability or the conversion program directly(Calibre-free download. A terrific program recommended by a Kindle Touch tech services guy. Wouldn't be without it!) The Kindle Touch when hooked to my home wireless network downloads web pages very fast. I can look up anything I need on Latin grammar from the web and even bookmark pages I want to save for later use. If I'm out and about I can find any free Wi Fi location and log on and do the same.

The things that are invaluable and a couple are unique to the Touch--the Fire, or the iPad 3 cannot do them, are:

1. Change the default dictionary to Latin, or any language for which you can get a digital dictionary that works with Kindle Touch. I have two Latin dictionaries that cost nearly nothing! This is a great help to anyone trying to translate and learn a new language. If I can't find it in the default ditionary I am using I then work the magic of...............

2. Web search for Latin words. I can get Google Translate, the Whitaker Latin Dictionary, Perseus Latin Word Search, etc through the browser. Pages I want to use often I can Bookmark and open them through the Menu screen for the Touch. Then, and this is crucial...........

3. You can expand browser pages by a couple of taps or by the expanding finger touch move on the screen. Many Latin words are displayed in tables that are actually images and are really too small to deal with. Just hold your finger/stylus on the screen, the box pops up and the little magnifying glass with + sign in it appears. Press that and Voila! the image now fills the screen in comfortable text size. This can be done with books too and makes tables of conjugated verbs, noun declensions etc from texts and web pages super readable and thus useful.

4. Notes. Press an word that I want to look up later, type a note about my thought(s) or that I want to translate off the web later on, save it and then look up later in View Notes and Marks for the document/book I am working with. A great way to study!

5. The reading screen is so comfortable to use. Absolutely no glare and I cannot say that about Kindle Fire or iPads--anti-glare covers are a necessity with them. Just try to read something with the Fire on sunny day while sitting in the car waiting for your spouse to get finished shopping. Not easy. With the Touch it is simplicity in itself. Just turn on and read.

6. Many books have an interactive "live" table of contents. If I really want that in a book I download a sample first and check. If it doesn't have one I may not buy although you can navigate with page/location numbers if necessary. Just a bit more awkward.

7. Amount of stuff on the device. I have over 4000 pages of the works of St. Thomas Aquinas, Aristotle's complete works of his major writings, again nearly 1000 pages, several very large Latin textbooks, other philosophy books, three different copies of the Bible, etc etc. Probably approaching 7-8000 pages of material ALL AT MY FINGERTIPS!........Plus the web when near Wi Fi and connected.

My wife received her Touch from me for her birthday. She is a voracious reader of thriller/mystery novels, the Vince Flynn, David Baldacci, et. al., genre. Since she got the Kindle Touch her reading speed has increased noticeably. She can make the type as large as she wants it to be, adjust the interlinear gap and look up words she doesn't know with the default English dictionary that comes with the device.

Finally, I can charge my Touch, use it everyday, web time, download time, reading time and a lot of just looking at the screen "think time" I charge it about every two weeks. She does the same, maybe less frequently because she doesn't make the Internet demands on her device that I do on mine. The Fire or the iPad--admittedly devices with much more capability for complex displays, videos, etc can make 7-10 hours before a charge is required. That can be a problem for people on the move.

I am sure I will find other great uses for this device. So far, I can find no knocks at all. My wife had to exchange her first machine because the touch screen wasn't quite right. That was a snap. I have contacted Kindle Customer/Technical Service Support about 7-8 times with questions or wanting to return her first device(which was replaced with the new one by overnight shipment!!!!!!!!!!! At no charge. Had the new one before we had to send the old one back. That is customer service.) The people I have talked to are well-trained, smart, very easy to talk to and polite beyond my experience on the web. Amazon customer service is superior. That is a major selling point as well.

I do not work for Amazon, never heard of them until a few years ago and nobody has helped me learn to use my Touch or my wife's either beyond a few calls about things that were actually easy to take care of if I had only read the right page of the manual. I would buy Touch again in a second! At $99 for the one with ads, which I have, or my wife's without ads at $139 there is not better reading/study device available outside of a full-fledged laptop/desktop computer, and I hate to sit in front of them all day anyhow.

Thank you Amazon. You have scored 10+
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Wired Keyboard 600 (Black). Wired Keyboard for Gaming Experience. USB Connectivity. Spill Resistant Design. This is a very basic keyboard, but it gets nearly everything right. The layout adheres to the QUERTY convention, it has illuminated indicators for caps and num lock, it has a numeric keypad, and basic multimedia controls (play/pause and volume). It covers all of the bases for a basic keyboard.

The key feel is nice. It's quiet, and the keys are comfortable to press. The function keys are smaller than the other keys to save on space but work just fine. The attached USB cord is nice and long (about 6 foot). The overall build quality feels decently solid for the price point. It auto installed on Win 10 without a hitch.

Misses are minor. It lacks a sleep button. It has a calculator button instead that, for me, is far less useful than a sleep button. It also lacks non-slip pads on the base. There are two legs that can be used to prop up the keyboard, but the keyboard is so light that it's easy to shift the position of it in use. I solved it with some stick-on non-slip material.

I've always used Microsoft keyboards and have yet to have one fail on me. There are other basic keyboards that are a dollar or two less expensive than this, but considering this is less than $11, I'd rate the overall value as very good. If you're looking for a basic, everyday keyboard and don't need/want anything fancy, this will fit the bill well and do so at a great price. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wired Keyboard 600 (Black). Wired Keyboard for Gaming Experience. USB Connectivity. Spill Resistant Design.

Soundcore by Anker Life Q30 Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Multiple Modes, Hi-Res Sound, Custom EQ via App, 40H Playtime, Comfortable Fit, Bluetooth Headphones, Multipoint Connection These are very good travel headphones. Over-the-ear style is very comfortable when worn for hours at a time. The headphones are relatively lightweight and compact. They fold nicely into the included EVA soft-shell case, which fits easily into my carry-on bag.

The headphones pair easily with my Android smartphone. The Soundcore smartphone app is required for upgrading the headphones' firmware. The app also lets you customize the equalization to one of the presets or you can design your own. Depending on the kind of music you are listening to, the equalizer can make a noticeable difference in clarity and balance.

Unfortunately, the app spams me with notifications about unrelated Anker products. Hopefully this will not be frequent.

Noise cancellation works well. There are 3 modes: on, off (normal), and transparency that lets you talk to people around you without taking the headphones off. Noise cancellation can be toggled both from the app and from a button on the headphones themselves.

Overall, sound quality is good. More of a balanced sound than the boomy default effects that some headphones give. I mostly listen to acoustic music, so this works well for me. Clarity is good. Bluetooth connectivity has been great so far.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore by Anker Life Q30 Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Multiple Modes, Hi-Res Sound, Custom EQ via App, 40H Playtime, Comfortable Fit, Bluetooth Headphones, Multipoint Connection

text_fidelity_a:
Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black Before you buy, check the Monoprice website for this item. The price may be much cheaper over there.

This is a very inexpensive, relatively low quality TV antenna. You get what you pay for. They advertise this for both indoor and outdoor use, but the mostly plastic construction will not last long outdoors in areas that get a lot of wind, ice, or bright sunlight. The attached 3 foot cable really tells you what their intended use case is. If your TV is near a window, hang the antenna in the window, plug it in, and you're done.

The advertised 50 mile range is for ideal conditions, mounting the antenna outdoors in an area where there are absolutely no obstructions between your home and the TV broadcast tower (no trees, no buildings, etc). Expect much worse range for an indoor mounting and if there are any obstructions. If you live in an area with trees etc, you should get a more sturdy antenna that can be mounted on a pole on top of your roof so it can receive a signal over the trees.

This antenna is advertised for UHF frequencies only. Most TV stations use UHF these days, but in my area there are a couple that use VHF and this antenna is not usable for those channels. If you really want VHF, I suggest getting a different antenna from this one.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black

For me, this is essential to avoid neck strain as well as the picture distortion I experienced when I was using a vertical monitor placement.

The quality of the picture and overall screen resolution for this monitor is excellent. There is slightly more glare than I prefer, but not enough to be truly uncomfortable to my eyes.

The design of the monitor is extremely attractive. It has a very sleek, modern look, and the frame around the monitor looks like a good-quality picture frame. I had no trouble assembling this monitor, even though I am not particularly handy, because all I needed to do was snap on the base of the stand.

The monitor comes with a power cable and a VGA cable. They are of standard specifications and would fit most any monitor. Conversely, most standard cables will fit on this monitor, as well. In fact, I didn't bother removing the cables that I had used for my old monitor when hooking up this new monitor to my computer, since they worked just fine. I stored the the new cables in the event they old cables break at some point.

All in all, I am very satisfied with my purchase.

Update 12/10/13: I just spent 30 minutes on the phone with ASUS support regarding some issues with the monitor which, interestingly, I ultimately figured out myself. The monitor's resolution had suddenly gone wildly out of whack, and there were dancing pixels all over the screen. The support technician was very friendly, and extremely helpful, but he went through a whole bunch of settings suggestions without ever thinking of asking about the cables. It turns out the VGA cable had come loose. (This kind of reminds me of long ago, in the early days of television, when you could call a TV repairman to your house. The first thing he would invariably do was to check and see if the TV was plugged in.)

text_fidelity_a:
Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver After an attempt to use [[ASIN:B005INJ4ZG My Zone Wireless Headphones]] was a bust for me due to its terrible sound quality, my techie husband bought this amp for me as part of a setup that allows me to listen to TV as loud as I want without disturbing him or the neighbors.

I directly hook up this amp to a head phone or earbuds when I am sitting close to the TV by using a special [[ASIN:B00009UVPN adapter]]. Head phones and earbuds have a 1/8 inch (3.5 mm) male jack (AKA male connector). Without an adapter, they can't be inserted into this amp, whose plug (AKA socket, female jack, or female connector) measures 1/4 inch (6.35 mm).

Because I like to move around my living room when I am watching TV, my husband also bought me a special [[ASIN:B0010CX798 male-to-female, headphone adapter, extension cable]]. The 1/4-inch, male jack of this cable fits into the 1/4-inch plug of this amp, and it has a 1/8-inch plug on its other end into which the jack of a head phone or ear bud can fit.

In order to use this setup, my husband also hooked into this amp a [[ASIN:B000068O3F male-to-male extension cable]]; one end is 1/8-inch and the other is 1/4-inch in diameter. The smaller end fits into a plug on the TV. When I want to use this external speaker source, I use the TV remote to access a menu that allows me to do that. Once this system is hooked up, I can no longer adjust the sound volume on the TV itself. I use the volume control on this amp.

Note that there is no On/Off switch on this amp. If you want to turn it off, so that you are not wasting electricity when it is not in use, you unhook the power cord from the far-left side of the amp.

This setup is a little complicated for the non-techie to figure out on their own, but if you have anyone techie in your family who can do it for you, it works really well.
text_fidelity_b: Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

I've likely tried every chemical variant of cleaner ever invented, though many fewer are now permitted for USA use.

Though impractical for the laptop, some excellent cleaners in the $1000/gal category might be suggested for cleansing strategic missile-related monitors and surfaces. The value and reliability of what device you are cleaning is the most critical consideration when choosing a cleaner. A wrong choice might pay back immediately with bad results, dissolving the anti-reflective coating or lamination of the touch screen overlay, removing specialized keyboard paints, ruining distinctive finishes, etc. For another, that same choice might do a bang-up job on the big screen at home, but when used on a laptop, it slowly dissolves and/or corrodes critical interconnects as you pass through dewpoints on that 17-hour airplane ride to Sydney.

Q: What is the best cleaner to shine on my $1500 laptop?

A: Not the cheapest $4/qt cleaner. Not one of grandma's window elixirs.

Behind the scenes, there is likely no other technical discussion as critical as cleaning and cleaners. Billions are spent every year on the problem. What I know from experience is that an alcohol solvent-based cleaner does a pretty good job erasing the symbology that makes my lighted keyboard legible. I look for a cleaner to remove the latent crusty-goo residue left by that anti-viral covid computer cleaner six months ago. Some cleaners with notionally benign saponifiers that sell under the enviro-friendly, "Green!", "non-GMO!" moniker is known to corrode solder joints and electro-plating to short the keyboard and LCD/OLED out.

Finding the right balance between solvent and saponifiers has not evolved smoothly. Saponifiers remove organics. The stuff that sprays out of your mouth and nose when yelling at the laptop. Solvents remove inorganics like hand cream, french fry grease, and Cheeto dust. I've rolled up all of this wisdom in my 'Rule #446 - Do not buy the cheapest electronics cleaner. Ever.'

This Monster cleaner is not cheap. It's a premium cleaner under a known premium brand. Given Monster brands, cleaning processes are the #1 priority for their established long-lived high-fidelity interconnection. My laptop has a touch screen that demands a non-delaminating cleaner and a lighted keyboard with that funky paint and laser-etched symbology. This Monster cleaner did an unexpectedly quick, no-smudge job on the laptop. All is good.
text_fidelity_b: Monster ScreenClean Soft Touch Wipes, Screen Cleaner Wipes for Computer Screens, TV, Phones, Tablets, and Car Touch Screens, Home Office, 70 Count

Sound Storm Labs SMC90BB Sound System Weatherproof Bluetooth Amplifier 3 Inch Speakers Inline Volume Control Ideal for Motorcycles ATV and 12 Volt Applications My husband put this on one of the farm Polaris CUV's since installation is beyond what I would able to do. He was able to install it on a ranger using the roof system as the mounting position for the speakers. It installed easily enough - basically clamp the speaker to the roof support bars, make sure to use the included rubber strips to get these to clamp securely or you will be remounting these with the rubber strips again once they slide down. Wiring was simple as it all goes to one plug that attaches to the amp. This does mean you will be mounting all 4 speakers. And since the wiring is together in a harness, some thought is required as to where you put the speakers and a good route to where you want the amp installed. The amp install is simple as it basically needs power (12vdc) and not a lot else. It does come with a handy audio input jack so you can use something like an old iPod for audio input. It also has BNC inputs if you have say a radio that you would want to connect to it so there is some flexibility there. The Bluetooth hook up was simple and works well, but again do not hide the amp behind a lot of metal or this may not work to well.

As far as fit and finish, the only thing I can knock this on is the quality of the clamping hardware finish, but being on a rough duty vehicle this is actually okay.

The bottom line is: Overall installation is simple, and the unit is easy to use.
text_fidelity_b: Sound Storm Labs SMC90BB Sound System Weatherproof Bluetooth Amplifier 3 Inch Speakers Inline Volume Control Ideal for Motorcycles ATV and 12 Volt Applications

text_fidelity_a:
Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple) [[VIDEOID:e832f455c8dfddb522ae3bbc1ec73698]] Loved the idea of an underwater camera for kids, and this one would have been great if not for the terrible image quality that would only disappoint any except maybe youngest of kids.

When I unpacked the box, I had great expectations. The waterproof shell seemed to be solid and to seal well, and there was a whole lot of extra parts to attach the camera to a bicycle and so on. Camera is very small, but the little screen is bright and it shows the image you're taking clearly. The interface is intuitive and reasonably simple. (I didn't bother to set the date before trying out the camera, but the instructions were clear, and I was able to test it with no problem, it works.)

HOWEVER: I can't believe how bad quality of the images are! They look jagged and pixelated like they're at 480 pixels. Even when I increased the quality in the settings to maximum image resolution, which is supposed to be 20Mb and 7344 pixels (more than what I shoot at for my professional photography biz), the quality stayed the same and the file size only crept up to just below 1 Meg. No idea how they managed to accomplish that. Their image sensor is at about the quality of those blurry, pixelated security cameras that are completely useless for identification. Otherwise, this camera focuses surprisingly well and handles a wide range of light conditions automatically. All the images were in a good range.

The video was marginally better, but still not what you'd expect at 1080 resolution. Camera was recognized by my Windows laptop right away, and I was able to access and copy images with no problem.

It's such a shame that the manufacturer decided to save money on image quality and it's a weird business decision that makes an otherwise fun and well built product useless.

Photos above were taken by the reviewed camera:
- The instruction manual image at highest resolution, and you can see its file size in the second screenshot image. Taken without the waterproof case.
- First Batman toy image at default resolution, without waterproof case
-Second Batman toy image at default resolution, with waterproof case on. Surprisingly, not much difference. Good plastic.
text_fidelity_b: Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser Momentum Headphone - Brown I've had several pairs of Sennheisers before the momentums namely a pair of HD580's from back in 1999 & much more recently a pair of HD650's. Let me start off by saying I'm not an "audiofile" I'm not a headphones snob. I don't name drop as to act like I know everything about all "cans" as they're referred to as. But I do know music & I know MY TYPE of music, which is pretty much everything except Country/Western. I listen 100% through my iphone or iPods.

I come from an LP, then 8 track (yuck), then cassette, then CD background so when I finally went all compressed format I didn't realize what I'd be "missing" I just thought, "Wow what a convenience"!! Anyway, I ended up ditching all my CD's (about 1400 total, originals!) & ripping them into iTunes, total of about 7500 songs. I long ago sold my HD580 back in 2005 & just listened from earbuds. I got tired of these real quick. So I saved up & did my research & just knew I had to have the Senn HD650's but I knew I had to have a good amp so I bought both (used) & I was thoroughly disappointed. I didn't hear this "wide open" expanded 3D imaged sound that everyone bragged about. After "damning" these headphones for being overpriced I realized, after my anger, I was being angry at the wrong item, it wasn't the can's it was the compressed format that removed all the subtle nuances of the original recordings!

So back to the drawing board to look for a decently priced (new) set of headphones. I bought a pair of in ear headphones from Sennhesier of course & these sounded good, better than than the Apple buds. Then I ran into the Momentums! I did my youtube & google research & the Momentums appear to be the one's I've been looking for. It has the controller but are "can" style headphones not earbuds! The cord is just long enough so i can stick my iphone in my pocket but no so long that it'll get caught on a doorknob or something else. The only drawback is it was hard to find the black with red from any type of discount. I got the brown ones reluctantly but I couldn't argue the price I got them for and for what it's worth the brown looks pretty clean & euro with the brushed aluminum.

I knew as soon as I started listening to some of the typical songs I play that I found my pair. They're paired perfectly for the portable MP3, phone or tablet's. You don't need an amp of any kind, they have great sound quality even for a sealed back design an because they're sealed you won't bother anyone sitting next to you at moderate levels. I was kind of put off of how small the ear surroundings were because my ears are not huge but they do stick out a bit, once I found a good position my ears fit fine.

All I can say is that I"m finally happy with a pair of headphones. I think the challenge is to match your style of music with headphones. Don't listen to name droppers & snobs who only talk about Gredo, AKG's HiFiMan & even Sennheisers. People knock Beats by Dre but hey if your music is like 99% current day hip hop & Dance then the Beats are probably the best suited for you. They're not for people who listen to live rock or classical. I had to find that out the hard way those higher priced headphones that require DAC's & AMPS aren't necessarily suited to my music. I believe the momentums are a great "in betweener" set of headphones. For that person who's aged a bit where they're not looking for LOUD & BOOM any more, they know & want detailed sound but they're still at a stage where they're listening to their music in a compressed 256k or less format, mp3 or wave format & not CD's anymore, but want that CD sound brought back.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser Momentum Headphone - Brown
